status: Replaces the WebRTC transport of file-manager-qualification-20261107.json. Measured on private stands. The installed result is in rdp-deployment-exp219-20261107.json.
change: File transfers moved from their own WebRTC connection to a WebSocket on the signal service's path, TCP 8006 with the gateway. The controller in the browser is the same one. The ceiling of aiortc is gone, and with it the stop of the ordered SCTP channel seen in 2 of 44 uploads.

fast_lan.path: 10 Gbit/s LAN, real PVE login and console popup, TLS through an HAProxy of the gateway's shape, signal, peer, terminal, helper in LXC 108. 1024 MiB each way, 3 runs.
fast_lan.ceiling: No node process is near a full core. About 100 MiB/s fills a 1 Gbit/s LAN but only a tenth of 10 Gbit/s. The browser is the likely limit: its main thread handles every frame beside the console, and the echo rises to 17-30 ms. Not proven by a run with a worker.

console_loop_during_a_fast_transfer.note: How late a 10 ms timer ran on the terminal's asyncio loop, which serves every console. The file session's threads share that process. p99 of each second, median over the phase, ms.

shaped_paths.note: Console in view, unloaded baselines first, then final code. Medians in ms. The bench's relay for the file session is plain TCP without HAProxy or TLS, which costs nothing measurable on these rates, and the file session runs in its own process, so these runs do not show its effect on the console's process (see console_loop_during_a_fast_transfer).

listing_during_a_transfer_ms.worst_where: An upload on 2 Mbit/s, 15 ms. It was 1669 on WebRTC.

vm_agent_requests_ms.note: Requests such as the clipboard's wait behind file lines on the one port. None failed.

defects_found_by_independent_review_and_: A silent TCP connection held the TLS handshake on the accepting thread and kept every new console out of a node without the gateway. It predates the file manager.
A file socket request with a made-up token reached the terminal, which runs every console's media.
Unanswered pings grew the peer's queue without limit, up to its address space limit.
A guest could flood lines that do nothing, and a partial line was searched again for every read.
A stalled media loop could leave a console refusing files until reopened.
A long listing ahead of file data on a narrow path ended the link as stalled.
A relink on a dead path could hang with Cancel doing nothing.
A long non-ASCII name could push a whole small file's frame over 65536 bytes.
A single download without a folder picker retried into its aborted spool, in memory.
open: A fast LAN reaches about 100 MiB/s, which fills 1 Gbit/s but not 10 Gbit/s.
On 2 Mbit/s a transfer costs the console about 10-20 ms, and an upload with 100 ms delay 15-25 ms.
The path's TCP is not ours: a lossy path behaves as TCP does there. Not measured.
A lost link still restarts the file from its beginning.
During an upload into a VM a clipboard request can wait about 200 ms (p95).
